 2027 NFL mock draft: Six quarterbacks go in the first round but none overcome Jeremiah Smith
 Six quarterbacks still come off the board in the first round even with Texas standout Arch Manning and Missouri passer Austin Simmons projected to stay in school
 By
 Josh Edwards 
 Nov 16, 2026
 at
 10:09 am ET 
 •
 1 min read
 Getty Images 
 The number of opportunities to make an impression on NFL talent evaluators this college football season may be as low as two for some prospects. The once vaunted 2027 NFL Draft class no longer appears as strong as it had in the summer, but there are still elite talents at the top. 
 In this thought exercise, the assumption is that Texas quarterback Arch Manning and Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons will return to school. The former has not reached his final form, and one would think his retired NFL uncles would encourage him to return to school until he is ready. However, there are still six quarterbacks taken in the first round. 
 The draft order is based on current win-loss records and strength of schedule was utilized for tiebreakers. It is also worth noting that five teams do not have a first-round pick, but each of those teams makes a pick below the first-round mock draft. 
 Without further ado, let's kick this off! 
 The 2027  NFL Draft  will take place April 29-May 1 at the National Mall in Washington, D.C. You can find more draft coverage at CBSSports.com, including weekly  mock drafts  and  updated prospect rankings . 
 NFL Mock Draft Round 1 
 Round 1 - Pick 1
 Jeremiah Smith 
 WR
 Ohio State
 • Jr
 • 6'4"
 / 222 lbs
 Projected Team
 L.A. Chargers 
 PROSPECT RNK
 1st
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 The Chargers do not seem motivated to move on from Justin Herbert, so quarterback is off the table. The decision is whether the team should take Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith or trade the right for another team to take a quarterback in exchange for a package of draft assets used to support a rebuild.
 Round 1 - Pick 2
 Leonard Moore 
 CB
 Notre Dame
 • Jr
 • 6'2"
 / 197 lbs
 Projected Team
 Tennessee 
 PROSPECT RNK
 2nd
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 If Los Angeles does not move off its pick, then Tennessee almost certainly would in a real-life situation. However, there is no point in adding another hypothetical when the point of the exercise is to provide insight into the best prospects eligible for the 2027 NFL Draft. Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore is a safer pick relative to South Carolina edge rusher Dylan Stewart and the suspension he has incurred this season.
 Round 1 - Pick 3
 Drew Mestemaker 
 QB
 Oklahoma State
 • Soph
 • 6'3"
 / 215 lbs
 Projected Team
 Miami 
 PROSPECT RNK
 4th
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 Miami has more problems than just quarterback Malik Willis, but Willis is not the future of the position, and the franchise must strike while the iron is hot. There are no guarantees in projecting college quarterbacks to the NFL, but Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker profiles as the most stable option among this year's crop.
 Round 1 - Pick 4
 Dylan Stewart 
 EDGE
 South Carolina
 • Jr
 • 6'5"
 / 250 lbs
 Projected Team
 N.Y. Jets 
 PROSPECT RNK
 3rd
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 Would New York take an edge rusher, No. 4 overall, one year after committing the No. 2 overall selection to the position? They should if that player is the best option. The Jets are not in a position to turn up their noses at a position of greater need.
 Round 1 - Pick 5
 Colin Simmons 
 EDGE
 Texas
 • Jr
 • 6'3"
 / 246 lbs
 Projected Team
 Philadelphia 
 PROSPECT RNK
 3rd
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 Philadelphia will almost certainly address the trenches. The offensive line has deteriorated and the edge rushers have not delivered. There has not been an offensive lineman to justify such early consideration, so the choice is Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons.
   From
 Indianapolis Colts 
 Round 1 - Pick 6
 CJ Carr 
 QB
 Notre Dame
 • Jr
 • 6'2"
 / 215 lbs
 Projected Team
 N.Y. Jets 
 PROSPECT RNK
 10th
 POSITION RNK
 2nd
 New York may not be comfortable bypassing a quarterback at No. 4 overall if there is one they like, and truthfully, they would still have a choice between Texas' Colin Simmons or South Carolina's Dylan Stewart if they had gone with the quarterback first. Notre Dame's C.J. Carr is not a dynamic athlete, but he has been a surgeon, operating with precision in the pass game.
 Round 1 - Pick 7
 Darian Mensah 
 QB
 Miami (Fla.)
 • Jr
 • 6'3"
 / 205 lbs
 Projected Team
 Arizona 
 PROSPECT RNK
 81st
 POSITION RNK
 8th
 Arizona is trotting out a new starting quarterback seemingly every week. A lack of confidence in starting Carson Beck to this point does not inspire a lot of confidence. If the quarterback of the future is not on the roster, then bring in a quarterback who has won at every step.
 Round 1 - Pick 8
 Jordan Seaton 
 OT
 LSU
 • Jr
 • 6'5"
 / 311 lbs
 Projected Team
 Atlanta 
 PROSPECT RNK
 11th
 POSITION RNK
 2nd
 The plan at right tackle has been flawlessly executed and Jake Matthews is not getting any younger. LSU's Jordan Seaton is not a finished product but he profiles as the franchise left tackle.
 Round 1 - Pick 9
 Xavier Gilliam 
 DL
 Tennessee
 • Jr
 • 6'2"
 / 305 lbs
 Projected Team
 Houston 
 PROSPECT RNK
 6th
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 There are bigger needs than the interior defensive line, but Tennessee defensive tackle Xavier Gililam would be one of the best players available and the long-term pairing of last year's second-round selection, Kayden McDonald, and Gilliam would be entertaining.
 Round 1 - Pick 10
 Charlie Becker 
 WR
 Indiana
 • Jr
 • 6'4"
 / 208 lbs
 Projected Team
 Tampa Bay 
 PROSPECT RNK
 9th
 POSITION RNK
 2nd
 Indiana's Charlie Becker is 6-foot-4 and fast. He's not the bully that Mike Evans had been, but the size is beneficial to Baker Mayfield. Emeka Egbuka and Becker would be the duo of the future. The other consideration would be reinvesting in the defensive line, but Becker is a higher-rated prospect.
 Round 1 - Pick 11
 Chris Cole 
 LB
 Georgia
 • Jr
 • 6'3"
 / 235 lbs
 Projected Team
 New Orleans 
 PROSPECT RNK
 16th
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 Georgia's Chris Cole is pound-for-pound one of the greatest athletes in this draft class. The linebacker position is often not one to jump-start a rebuild, but Cole possesses that level of talent.
 Round 1 - Pick 12
 Ashton Hampton 
 CB
 Clemson
 • Jr
 • 6'2"
 / 205 lbs
 Projected Team
 Washington 
 PROSPECT RNK
 7th
 POSITION RNK
 2nd
 Washington would love to see Indiana wide receiver Charlie Becker available but, faced with the options available, Clemson cornerback Ashton Hampton is a more reasonable choice. Hampton is a bigger cornerback with good ball production throughout his collegiate career.
   From
 Dallas Cowboys 
 Round 1 - Pick 13
 Will Echoles 
 DL
 Ole Miss
 • Jr
 • 6'3"
 / 315 lbs
 Projected Team
 N.Y. Jets 
 PROSPECT RNK
 13th
 POSITION RNK
 2nd
 The Jets' haul of South Carolina edge rusher Dylan Stewart, Notre Dame quarterback C.J. Carr and Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles would be an exciting haul in New York. The defense has been a bigger issue for the team this season, so they address those concerns in the first round.
 Round 1 - Pick 14
 Nick Marsh 
 WR
 Indiana
 • Jr
 • 6'3"
 / 210 lbs
 Projected Team
 Las Vegas 
 PROSPECT RNK
 62nd
 POSITION RNK
 7th
 Indiana wide receiver Nick Marsh is a big body that Las Vegas has missed in the pass game; aside from how they use Brock Bowers. To explain the objective in a way that Fernando Mendaoza would understand, the Marsh selection is the equivalent of taking the answer to the question from a single-response question to a select-all-that-apply question.
 Round 1 - Pick 15
 Ellis Robinson IV 
 CB
 Georgia
 • Jr
 • 6'0"
 / 180 lbs
 Projected Team
 Baltimore 
 PROSPECT RNK
 24th
 POSITION RNK
 3rd
 Marlon Humphrey is not much longer for Baltimore and Nate Wiggins has not yet lived up to the promise he displayed as a rookie. Georgia cornerback Ellis Robinson IV was the nation's No. 2 high school recruit out of high school and now goes wire-to-wire as a top draft pick.
 Round 1 - Pick 16
 Jadan Baugh 
 RB
 Florida
 • Jr
 • 6'1"
 / 225 lbs
 Projected Team
 New England 
 PROSPECT RNK
 19th
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 It does not seem as though New England has a running back they trust and that can give them everything they want out of the position. Jadan Baugh is a bigger back who will retain some of the physical element in the offense.
 Round 1 - Pick 17
 Yhonzae Pierre 
 EDGE
 Alabama
 • Sr
 • 6'4"
 / 251 lbs
 Projected Team
 Seattle 
 PROSPECT RNK
 47th
 POSITION RNK
 8th
 Seattle is re-stocking the cupboard of edge rushers. Boye Mafe is gone and Yhonzae Pierre steps in as depth alongside Uchenna Nwosu and Derrick Hall.
   From
 Los Angeles Rams 
 Round 1 - Pick 18
 Dante Moore 
 QB
 Oregon
 • Sr
 • 6'3"
 / 220 lbs
 Projected Team
 Cleveland 
 PROSPECT RNK
 45th
 POSITION RNK
 5th
 In this scenario, three quarterbacks are off the board and the assumption is that Missouri's Austin Simmons and Texas' Arch Manning return to school. Cleveland would be faced with a choice of South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers, Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss and Oregon's Dante Moore. There is no question Sellers is a better athlete at the position, but Moore is a more consistent option, which the franchise may prefer.
 Round 1 - Pick 19
 Greg Johnson 
 IOL
 Minnesota
 • Sr
 • 6'6"
 / 325 lbs
 Projected Team
 Carolina 
 PROSPECT RNK
 14th
 POSITION RNK
 2nd
 Carolina could move on from Robert Hunt in the offseason and save $14 million toward the salary cap. The Panthers' offensive line has the second-highest pressure rate allowed this season, according to TruMedia. Minnesota's Greg Johnson would bring stability to the unit.
 Round 1 - Pick 20
 Boubacar Traore 
 EDGE
 Notre Dame
 • Sr
 • 6'5"
 / 253 lbs
 Projected Team
 Cleveland 
 PROSPECT RNK
 29th
 POSITION RNK
 6th
 With its second of two choices, Cleveland addresses its pass rush with the selection of Notre Dame's Boubacar Traore. Jared Verse has not yet delivered what the team expected when it acquired him as part of the Myles Garrett deal.
   From
 Green Bay Packers 
 Round 1 - Pick 21
 Trey'Dez Green 
 TE
 LSU
 • Jr
 • 6'7"
 / 242 lbs
 Projected Team
 Dallas 
 PROSPECT RNK
 30th
 POSITION RNK
 2nd
 Dallas will have a decision to make regarding wide receiver George Pickens, who is playing out the franchise tag. The addition of LSU tight end Trey'Dez Green would give them another big body in the passing game.
 Round 1 - Pick 22
 Cam Coleman 
 WR
 Texas
 • Jr
 • 6'3"
 / 204 lbs
 Projected Team
 N.Y. Giants 
 PROSPECT RNK
 17th
 POSITION RNK
 3rd
 Carnell Tate had been a consideration for New York but was taken one pick earlier. Malachi Fields has developed into a nice piece for the offense and, honestly, John Harbaugh may prefer to utilize assets elsewhere, but the idea of Cam Coleman, Malik Nabers and Fields is exciting.
 Round 1 - Pick 23
 LaNorris Sellers 
 QB
 South Carolina
 • Jr
 • 6'3"
 / 238 lbs
 Projected Team
 Pittsburgh 
 PROSPECT RNK
 121st
 POSITION RNK
 11th
 Aaron Rodgers has stated his intention to retire after the season, and there is not a lot of confidence in Drew Allar or Will Howard. LaNorris Sellers is a big body who will be difficult to bring down in the pocket, much like Ben Roethlisberger was.
 Round 1 - Pick 24
 Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa 
 LB
 Notre Dame
 • Jr
 • 6'3"
 / 230 lbs
 Projected Team
 Denver 
 PROSPECT RNK
 36th
 POSITION RNK
 2nd
 Denver had attempted to address its linebacker issues by signing free agent Dre Greenlaw. The Broncos return to the well for Notre Dame linebacker Kyngston Viliamu-Asa.
 Round 1 - Pick 25
 Zereoue Williams 
 OT
 Utah
 • Sr
 • 6'8"
 / 305 lbs
 Projected Team
 Cincinnati 
 PROSPECT RNK
 93rd
 POSITION RNK
 11th
 Amarius Mims has been excellent at right tackle for the Bengals, but Orlando Brown's play on the left side has diminished and the team would have an opportunity to save $7 million against the salary cap.
   From
 Jacksonville Jaguars 
 Round 1 - Pick 26
 Trevor Lauck 
 OT
 Iowa
 • Sr
 • 6'5"
 / 314 lbs
 Projected Team
 Philadelphia 
 PROSPECT RNK
 38th
 POSITION RNK
 6th
 As noted with the first of Philadelphia's two selections, the Eagles will almost certainly aim to replenish the trenches. After taking Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons earlier, the team circles back with a talent across the line of scrimmage: Iowa offensive lineman Trevor Lauck.
 Round 1 - Pick 27
 Trinidad Chambliss 
 QB
 Ole Miss
 • Sr
 • 6'0"
 / 210 lbs
 Projected Team
 Minnesota 
 PROSPECT RNK
 22nd
 POSITION RNK
 4th
 Minnesota made the move to re-acquire Kirk Cousins, who would be 39 years old prior to next season. The Vikings may not be enamored with going down the path of taking another small quarterback, but options are limited when a team is picking so late in the round.
   From
 Chicago Bears 
 Round 1 - Pick 28
 Lance Heard 
 OT
 Kentucky
 • Sr
 • 6'6"
 / 325 lbs
 Projected Team
 Tennessee 
 PROSPECT RNK
 20th
 POSITION RNK
 3rd
 Tennessee would save roughly $10 million by moving on from left tackle Dan Moore Jr. this offseason while upgrading in the process. Lance Heard has improved in pass protection but butter his bread in the run game.
 Round 1 - Pick 29
 Reed Harris 
 WR
 Arizona State
 • Sr
 • 6'5"
 / 220 lbs
 Projected Team
 Kansas City 
 PROSPECT RNK
 108th
 POSITION RNK
 13th
 Kansas City acquired Josh Downs at the trade deadline, but the team is still sorely lacking in the size department. The Chiefs would benefit from having a player on the boundary who can win above the rim.
 Round 1 - Pick 30
 Kelley Jones 
 CB
 Mississippi State
 • Sr
 • 6'4"
 / 205 lbs
 Projected Team
 Detroit 
 PROSPECT RNK
 27th
 POSITION RNK
 4th
 Detroit has played most of the season without the majority of its expected starting secondary. They have made some small changes, but the long-term outlook remains grim. Kelley Jones is a lengthy cornerback with ball production.
 Round 1 - Pick 31
 Jamari Johnson 
 TE
 Oregon
 • Sr
 • 6'5"
 / 255 lbs
 Projected Team
 San Francisco 
 PROSPECT RNK
 25th
 POSITION RNK
 1st
 Trying to time when San Francisco will address the replacements for key components like offensive tackle Trent Williams and tight end George Kittle is like trying to buy the dip in the stock market. Every time you think one or the other is going to retire, they return for more. The selection of Oregon tight end Jamari Johnson is once again an effort to bridge the present to the future.
 Round 1 - Pick 32
 Anthonie Knapp 
 IOL
 Notre Dame
 • Jr
 • 6'5"
 / 305 lbs
 Projected Team
 Buffalo 
 PROSPECT RNK
 83rd
 POSITION RNK
 8th
 If there had been an obvious option at wide receiver, that would have been a consideration, but fortifying the offensive line is more appealing when exploring the options available.
 Teams without a first-round pick
 38. Indianapolis Colts: WR KJ Duff, Rutgers
 Indianapolis traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, leaving them essentially with Alec Pierce. The Colts are going to need more help at the position.
 49. Los Angeles Rams: OT Melvin Siani, Texas
 One criticism of Los Angeles' draft approach last season was not using a Top-100 pick on an offensive tackle, even though Alaric Jackson had been dealing with off-field problems. 
 53. Green Bay Packers: OT Carter Smith, Indiana
 Indiana's Carter Smith could play guard or tackle, which is a quality Green Bay often looks for among its offensive line. 
 61. Chicago Bears: LB Sammy Brown, Clemson
 It would not be a surprise if Ben Johnson continued throwing resources at wide receiver or running back, but linebacker may prove to be a bigger need. 
 91. Jacksonville Jaguars: CB Jalen Mayo, Houston
 Jacksonville addressed safety and the defensive interior at the trade deadline, but cornerback opposite Travis Hunter Jr. is a question mark.
